staging.hold_reason: WP-373 adds 0089: it schedules the lease sweeper that 0082 defined but never wired up. Paired with the client's new 60s heartbeat, a live run keeps its lease while it runs and a crashed device's run is closed within a minute instead of staying 'running' forever. Schema is unchanged - the migration only creates one pg_cron job. Staging applies first so production repeats a proven step.

backup_waiver.reason: Free plan project has no daily backup and no PITR; owner accepted production apply with no rollback path.

production.hold_reason: HOLD - 0089 is applied on all three environments (production apply run 30307084863, post-check head 0089 on jiphfrpzvkpzubbkhrwb; staging run 30303743005). The gate is reclosed by policy: any further production migration needs its own explicit owner GO. release_enabled stays false because cutting a stable tag requires separate owner approval. What 0089 does: it schedules the pg_cron job that runs select public.expire_global_timer_v2_leases(200) every minute - the sweeper 0082 defined but never wired up. No table, column, index, policy or grant changed and no row was inserted. Rollback is a single cron.unschedule with no client release. The backup waiver stays recorded because the project still has no PITR or daily backup; it is a waiver, not a standing apply permission. Note that the client half of WP-373 is what actually fixes multi-device timer sync - both devices need the new build; 0089 is only the crash-safety net.
